events.title: Disaster Strikes the Royal Navy off the Isles of Scilly
events.description: A fleet returning from the Mediterranean was caught in stormy weather and misjudged its position. Four Royal Navy ships were wrecked off the Isles of Scilly, and at least 1,400 sailors died.
events.significance: It was one of the worst maritime disasters in British history. It led directly to the Longitude Act of 1714, which spurred the search for a reliable way to measure longitude at sea.

events.title: The Great Disappointment
events.description: Followers of the preacher William Miller had predicted that Christ would return on this day. When nothing happened, thousands of Millerites were left shaken.
events.significance: Out of the aftermath came new religious movements, including the Seventh-day Adventist Church, which still has millions of members.

events.title: The Metropolitan Opera House Opens in New York
events.description: The Metropolitan Opera opened its first house on Broadway at 39th Street with a performance of Gounod's Faust.
events.significance: The Met became one of the world's leading opera companies and a lasting center of American musical life.

events.title: Kennedy Reveals Soviet Missiles in Cuba
events.description: In a televised address, President John F. Kennedy told Americans that Soviet missile sites had been found in Cuba. He announced a naval quarantine of the island.
events.significance: The speech brought the Cuban Missile Crisis into public view. The standoff was the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war.
